# tool-guardian

> Router that fronts your MCP servers behind 6 small tools so their schemas stay out of the context window. Python 3.9+, standard library only, MIT.

Run it as a single stdio MCP server; your real servers sit behind it and the model reaches them through `call_tool`.

## Install

- Any MCP client, nothing to install: `uvx tool-guardian --version`
- Installed: `pip install tool-guardian`, then run `tool-guardian`
- Add a server it should route: `uvx --from tool-guardian tool-guardian-setup add NAME -- COMMAND ARGS...` (or `tool-guardian-setup import` to copy servers from Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf)
- Register it with the client, e.g. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user tool-guardian -- uvx tool-guardian`
- Check it: `uvx tool-guardian --selftest` (expect `N backend(s) up, M tools reachable.`)
- DeepSeek Harness only: the npm package `dsh-tool-guardian` is a DSH bundle, installed with `dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-tool-guardian` (it is not an `npx` command)
- Full steps: [Install](README.md#install) and [Quick start](README.md#quick-start-60-seconds)

## Configure

- Config is the standard `mcpServers` block: `{"mcpServers": {"files": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/data"]}}}`
- Search order: `--config PATH`, then `$TOOL_GUARDIAN_CONFIG`, then `~/.tool-guardian/mcp.json`.
- A config in the current directory (`./mcp.json`, `./.mcp.json`) is NOT loaded without the user's consent, because a cloned repo can carry one. Do not enable it for the user; ask first. To opt in: `--config ./mcp.json`, `TOOL_GUARDIAN_CONFIG=./mcp.json`, or `TOOL_GUARDIAN_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`.
- stdio and remote Streamable HTTP servers (`"url"`, 2026-07-28 or 2025-11-25/06-18/03-26) are routed; `"type": "sse"` is `UNSUPPORTED` until 0.9.1; no OAuth (see Remote servers).
- Details: [Configure](README.md#configure), [Run](README.md#run), [Troubleshooting](README.md#troubleshooting)

## Tools

- `list_capabilities`: tool names with one-line summaries for one server or all; start here
- `search_capabilities`: find a tool by keyword across servers
- `describe_tool`: the arguments of one tool (`detail=full` for its whole schema)
- `call_tool`: run a backend tool (`server`, `tool`, `args`) and return its shaped result
- `list_groups_with_costs`: tool groups and the context-token cost of loading each
- `retrieve_spill`: read back the full original of a shortened result
- Reference: [Tools](README.md#tools)
